component.name: Lightmorphic Flow
component.summary: Share one mouse, keyboard and clipboard between computers

description.p: Lightmorphic Flow lets one keyboard and mouse drive up to four other computers on the same network, one on each edge of your screen, and keeps the text clipboard in step between them.

It never takes over a screen edge. A light touch on an edge or a corner does nothing at all, so hot corners and hot edges carry on working the way they always did. Only a deliberate, continued push moves the pointer to the next computer. While the pointer is on your own screen nothing is grabbed, so touchpad gestures, pointer speed and every shortcut are untouched.
The computers find each other by themselves, and every link is encrypted.
This is a beta release. Expect rough edges.

description.p: A full review: reports keep secrets out, the pairing door shuts behind one machine, the touchpad drives the pointer too, and nothing can reach two machines at once after a stall.
Exit in the tray menu stops the whole app.
Flow now drives the main computer's pointer itself, so it always knows where it is and never crosses early.
The pointer no longer jumps to the other computer before it has reached the edge.
GNOME's hot corner opens the Overview on the computer being controlled.
Clicking the update dot no longer maximises the window.
Only the edge facing your main computer brings the pointer home, so the other computer's own hot corners and edges work, and the tray icon shows on GNOME.
Finds the other computer even when a strict firewall is running.
Crossing over no longer feels like pushing through a wall.
The shared clipboard works on GNOME with Wayland, and crossing over is less fussy.
Crossing over works the second time and every time after, not only the first.
Letting go of the mouse and keyboard now really lets go, so the computer you are sitting at never locks up after the pointer comes home.
The pointer should now move on the receiving computer, with a switch to fall back if it does not.
Says plainly when the two computers are running versions that cannot work together, instead of half working.
Coming home is now a nudge rather than a shove, so the pointer never feels stuck on the other machine.
The pointer can find its way back from the other machine, and the clipboard needs no other programs installed.
Says when the other computer's identity has changed instead of retrying silently, and stops the tray flashing in the dock.
Finds computers on home networks that are not the usual size, and an upgrade now restarts what is running.
Something that cannot start now gives up instead of flashing in the dock for ever.
No more stray flickering icon in the dock.
Records exactly what happens when the pointer crosses and comes back, including whether the mouse was really let go of.
The pointer no longer bounces straight back the moment it crosses, and the tray icon stops flickering.
Logs what it is doing as it happens, and writes a full report you can send on.
The computer you are sitting at can no longer be left frozen with its mouse and keyboard held.
The computer being controlled now asks, so a firewall on it needs no change at all.
Says when a firewall is stopping the computers seeing each other, and offers to open it for you.
Allowing a new computer counts down in the row itself. No popups.
The tray icon appears without waiting for the next login, and its menu connects and disconnects.
It works the moment it is installed. No logging out and back in.
Screenshots and a proper listing in every software centre.
It now tells you, in a dialog you have to acknowledge, that you must log out and back in before it can read your mouse and keyboard.
The doctor reports the tray library correctly.
The update dot appears on Fedora: the drawing library it needs is now asked for.
A doctor command, and the update dot can no longer vanish silently.
The update dot follows the revised house standard.
The update dot sits opposite the logo again.
A tray icon that shows where the pointer is, lets you send it to any of your computers, and turns sharing on and off.
The update dot follows the house standard exactly.
The application icon and the listing in your software centre.
Finds other computers on the network. Drives up to four at once.
